cards.front: What happens to your privilege after a homicide or aggravated assault involving a vehicle?
cards.back: Any homicide or aggravated assault involving the use of a vehicle leads to revocation of your driving privilege.

cards.front: What does any felony committed with a vehicle lead to?
cards.back: Any felony committed with the use of a vehicle leads to revocation.

cards.front: What does lying under oath about who owns or operates a vehicle lead to?
cards.back: Lying under oath about who owns or operates a vehicle leads to revocation.

cards.front: What does failing to stop and give aid at a crash you are in lead to?
cards.back: Failing to stop and give aid at the scene of a traffic crash you are involved in leads to revocation.

cards.front: What do two or more DUI convictions lead to?
cards.back: Having two or more DUI convictions leads to revocation.

cards.front: What does an aggravated DUI conviction lead to?
cards.back: An aggravated DUI conviction leads to revocation.

cards.front: What does causing a death or serious physical injury with a vehicle lead to?
cards.back: Causing a death or serious physical injury by using a vehicle leads to revocation.

cards.front: How do repeat DUI convictions and repeat reckless driving convictions differ?
cards.back: Two or more DUI convictions bring revocation, while two or more reckless driving or racing convictions bring suspension.

cards.front: What may happen if you do not take and pass a required driving retest?
cards.back: Your privilege may also be revoked if you do not take and pass a driving retest that you were required to take.

cards.front: What may happen if you are found unable to operate a motor vehicle?
cards.back: Your privilege may be revoked if you are found medically, psychologically or physically unable to operate a motor vehicle.

cards.front: What may happen if your continued driving would endanger public safety?
cards.back: Your privilege may be revoked if your continued driving would endanger public health, safety or welfare.

decks.domain: Revocation and suspension grounds, vehicle impound, violation points and Traffic Survival School, chemical test refusal, financial responsibility, failure to appear and traffic ticket enforcement

cards.front: What do two or more reckless driving or racing convictions lead to?
cards.back: Two or more convictions for reckless driving, or two or more for racing on the highways, lead to suspension of your driving privilege.

cards.front: What is suspension?
cards.back: Suspension is the temporary removal of your driving privilege, taken after a review of your driving record or when the law requires it.

cards.front: Is a suspension for repeat reckless driving permanent?
cards.back: Repeat reckless driving or racing convictions bring a suspension, which is only a temporary removal of the privilege.

cards.front: What do you pay after a suspension?
cards.back: After a suspension you pay the reinstatement fee plus the license application fee for your age group.

cards.front: When must a vehicle be impounded or immobilized because of the driver's privilege?
cards.back: A vehicle must be impounded or immobilized when the driver's privilege is suspended or revoked for any reason.

cards.front: When must a vehicle be impounded because the driver was never licensed?
cards.back: A vehicle must be impounded or immobilized when the driver has never held a valid license or permit and cannot show an out-of-state license.

cards.front: When must a vehicle be impounded because of an ignition interlock?
cards.back: A vehicle must be impounded or immobilized when a driver who must use an ignition interlock device is driving without a working certified device.

cards.front: What adds points to your permanent driving record?
cards.back: Every conviction or bail forfeiture for a moving traffic violation adds points to your permanent driving record.

cards.front: What happens if you build up eight or more points within twelve months?
cards.back: If you build up eight or more points within any twelve-month period, you must attend Traffic Survival School, or your privilege may be suspended.

cards.front: What is the points threshold for Traffic Survival School?
cards.back: The points threshold for Traffic Survival School is eight or more points, counted inside any twelve-month period.

cards.front: Which violations carry eight points?
cards.back: DUI, extreme DUI, aggravated DUI, reckless driving, racing on highways and aggressive driving each carry eight points.

cards.front: How many points does leaving the scene of a crash carry?
cards.back: Leaving the scene of a crash carries six points.

cards.front: How many points does failing to stop or yield carry when it causes a death?
cards.back: Failing to stop for a signal or stop sign, or failing to yield the right-of-way, carries six points when it causes a death.

cards.front: How many points does failing to stop or yield carry when it causes serious injury?
cards.back: Failing to stop for a signal or stop sign, or failing to yield the right-of-way, carries four points when it causes serious injury.

cards.front: Which violations carry six points, and which carry four?
cards.back: Leaving the scene of a crash and a failure to stop or yield that causes death each carry six points, while the same failure causing serious injury carries four points.
cards.memory_hook: six scene or death, four injury

cards.front: How many points does a speeding violation carry?
cards.back: A speeding violation carries three points.

cards.front: How many points does driving over or parking in a gore area carry?
cards.back: Driving over or parking in a gore area carries three points.

cards.front: How many points does wrong-way driving carry?
cards.back: Wrong-way driving carries two points, the same as every other moving violation not listed separately.

cards.front: Which violations carry three points, and which carry two?
cards.back: Speeding and gore-area violations each carry three points, while wrong-way driving and all other moving violations carry two points.
cards.memory_hook: three speed or gore, two others

cards.front: What does a conviction for running a red light make mandatory?
cards.back: A conviction for running a red light or a flashing red light makes TSS mandatory on top of all court fines and fees.

decks.domain: Revocation and suspension grounds, vehicle impound, violation points and Traffic Survival School, chemical test refusal, financial responsibility, failure to appear and traffic ticket enforcement

cards.front: What may frequent serious traffic offenses lead to?
cards.back: MVD may suspend or revoke your privilege, or require TSS, if you are convicted of frequent serious traffic offenses that show disregard for the safety of others.

cards.front: What may a reckless driving conviction or repeat negligent driving lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of reckless driving or are a repeat reckless or negligent driver.

cards.front: What may fraudulent use of your driver license lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if you commit or allow an unlawful or fraudulent use of your driver license.

cards.front: What may a DUI conviction for alcohol, drugs or toxic vapors lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol, drugs or toxic vapors.

cards.front: What does refusing a chemical test bring?
cards.back: Refusing or failing to complete a chemical test for alcohol or drug content brings a twelve-month suspension, or two years for a second or later refusal within a seven-year period.

cards.front: How do first and repeat chemical test refusals differ?
cards.back: A first chemical test refusal brings a twelve-month suspension, while a second or later refusal within seven years brings two years.

cards.front: What may an unresolved judgment from another state lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if you have an unresolved judgment from another state.

cards.front: What may an offense requiring mandatory revocation lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if you commit an offense that requires mandatory revocation upon conviction.

cards.front: What may an alcohol conviction lead to for a driver under twenty-one?
cards.back: MVD may act against the license of a driver under twenty-one who is convicted of receiving, drinking or possessing alcohol.

cards.front: What may a drug conviction lead to for a driver under twenty-one?
cards.back: MVD may act against the license of a driver under twenty-one who is convicted of any illegal drug violation.

cards.front: What may being medically unsafe to drive lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if you are medically unsafe to drive.

cards.front: What may a conviction in a crash causing death, injury or serious damage lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if, as a driver, you are convicted in a crash that caused death, personal injury or serious property damage.

cards.front: What may violating a restriction on your license lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of violating a restriction on your license.

cards.front: What may failing to comply with an ignition interlock order lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if you fail to comply with a certified ignition interlock device order.

cards.front: What may a first moving violation lead to for a driver under eighteen?
cards.back: MVD may act against the license of a driver under eighteen who is convicted of a first moving civil traffic violation or certain criminal traffic offenses.

cards.front: What may wrong-way driving on a controlled-access highway lead to?
cards.back: MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of wrong-way driving on a controlled-access highway.

cards.front: In what two ways does wrong-way driving appear?
cards.back: Wrong-way driving appears both as a two-point violation and, on a controlled-access highway, as a ground for MVD action.

decks.module: Reinstatement, driving while suspended and insurance
decks.domain: Revocation and suspension grounds, vehicle impound, violation points and Traffic Survival School, chemical test refusal, financial responsibility, failure to appear and traffic ticket enforcement

cards.front: What must you do to reinstate after a suspension or revocation period?
cards.back: After a suspension or revocation period, you must pay the application fee to reinstate, and you may face an investigation and have to file an SR-twenty-two Certificate of Insurance.

cards.front: What may police do if you are cited for driving on a suspended license?
cards.back: If you are cited for driving on a suspended or revoked license, police may impound your vehicle for up to thirty days.

cards.front: What may you be eligible for after a conviction for driving on a suspended license?
cards.back: A person convicted of driving on a suspended or revoked license may be eligible for a restricted driver license.

cards.front: How do being cited and being convicted for driving while suspended differ?
cards.back: Being cited for driving while suspended can mean an impound of up to thirty days, while being convicted of it can make you eligible for a restricted license.

cards.front: What does a first proof-of-insurance violation bring?
cards.back: A first conviction for lacking or failing to show proof of current financial responsibility in the vehicle suspends the license, registration and plates for three months.

cards.front: What does a second proof-of-insurance violation within thirty-six months bring?
cards.back: A second financial responsibility violation within thirty-six months brings a six-month suspension of the license, registration and plates.

cards.front: What does a third or later proof-of-insurance violation within thirty-six months bring?
cards.back: A third or later financial responsibility violation within thirty-six months brings a one-year suspension of the license, registration and plates.

cards.front: How do financial responsibility suspensions grow?
cards.back: Financial responsibility suspensions rise from three months for a first violation to six months and then one year for repeat violations within thirty-six months.

cards.front: What happens if MVD learns you missed court or did not pay a criminal traffic charge?
cards.back: Your license will be suspended if MVD is told that you missed a court appearance or did not pay a criminal traffic violation charge.

cards.front: What does signing a traffic citation mean?
cards.back: Signing a traffic citation is your promise to appear in traffic court.

cards.front: For what court matters may a driver under eighteen be suspended?
cards.back: A driver under eighteen may have the privilege suspended for missing court, not paying a fine or not following any court order.

cards.front: Can a driver under eighteen be suspended for failing any court order?
cards.back: Drivers under eighteen can be suspended for failing any court order, not only for missing court or not paying a fine.

cards.front: What must MVD do when a court reports delinquent traffic fines?
cards.back: Courts report people who are behind on traffic or boating fines, or who missed a criminal traffic or boating case, and MVD must then block renewal of any vehicle registration they own.

cards.front: How do missed court and delinquent fines affect you?
cards.back: Missing court or not paying a criminal traffic charge suspends the license, while delinquent traffic fines also block vehicle registration renewal.

cards.front: What may a person under eighteen not use false ID to get?
cards.back: A person under eighteen may not use false identification to get someone to sell, serve, give or furnish a nitrous oxide container.

recap_hooks.text: Vehicular homicide, a felony with a vehicle, failing to give aid and repeat or aggravated DUI all lead to revocation.
Suspension is temporary; a vehicle must be impounded when the driver is suspended, revoked or never licensed.
Eight or more points in twelve months means TSS; speeding carries three points and wrong-way driving two.
MVD may act for DUI, test refusal, fraud and many other grounds; a first refusal costs twelve months.

recaps.module: Reinstatement, driving while suspended and insurance

recap_hooks.text: Insurance violations bring three months, then six months, then one year within thirty-six months.
Missing court or not paying a criminal traffic charge suspends your license, and a signed citation is a promise to appear.
